A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KIDOT research, with matching core methods and experiments. The text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–B support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original MRI and CT reconstruction results, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and statistical comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, discretization sensitivity, low-data experiments, and cross-anatomy and cross-contrast results.

M1.justification: The transport dynamics, neural backbones, implemented losses in Eqs. (10)–(12), and Algorithm 1 are retained. The added backbone rationale and discretization study document and test the existing framework without introducing a new reconstruction procedure.

E1.justification: The original simulated knee MRI, prospective brain MRI, and clinical CT coverage is retained. Appendix B.7 adds fastMRI knee-to-brain and T1-to-T2 brain reconstruction scenarios, substantially extending evaluation to anatomical and contrast shifts beyond the original sampling-mask mismatch.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 add FSBM to all three original benchmark comparisons. DDS is added to simulated MRI and, as pre-trained, from-scratch, and fine-tuned variants, to real MRI. Figure 3 replaces its zero-filling comparison panel with fine-tuned DDS; zero filling remains in appendix visuals.

E3.justification: New protocols include three DDS training strategies, 20% and 10% paired-training subsets, a sweep over N = 6, 9, 12, 15, and cross-domain training designs. In cross-anatomy evaluation, KIDOT receives unpaired high-quality knee and degraded brain data, whereas E2E-VarNet receives paired knee data. Existing benchmark splits, preprocessing, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained loss, gamma, lambda, and forward-operator ablations, v2 adds discretization sensitivity (Table 5), data-scarcity robustness (Table 10), anatomy/contrast shift analyses (Tables 11–12), and real-MRI training curves (Figure 7). These substantially broaden the questions investigated.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 retains the same per-image paired t-tests, bootstrap-based FID/KID testing, and p-values, with Table 8 becoming Table 9. No new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty analyses are reported for the added comparisons.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, but substantial new results appear. Table 2 adds fine-tuned DDS at FID 39.78 versus the unchanged KIDOT score of 28.26. New tables report an optimum at N = 12, low-data results, and cross-domain outcomes, including cross-anatomy PSNR 34.62 for KIDOT versus 33.82 for E2E-VarNet. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.2, their assumptions, and the appendix proofs are unchanged. Eq. (9) reverses the expectation difference, but this is an equivalent Wasserstein dual representation because the Lipschitz function class is closed under sign reversal.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about physics-informed dynamic transport, learning from unpaired data, solution existence, and MRI/CT reconstruction effectiveness. The added evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation by attributing data efficiency and cross-domain performance to physics-based regularization and reduced overfitting. It adds arguments that matched backbones isolate KIDOT's contribution and hypothesizes gradient instability as the cause of degradation at N = 15. The original forward-model availability and computational-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 only promises a future code release; v2 adds a repository URL in the abstract, although Appendix B.1 retains the future-release wording. Appendix B.3.1 newly specifies N = 12 as the default. Existing optimizer, learning-rate, hardware, and data-processing disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Joint Velocity-Growth Flow Matching, Feedback Schrödinger Bridge Matching, and Decomposed Diffusion Sampler. The background briefly positions FSBM as dynamic transport for semi-supervised problems. The broader related-work narrative and claimed novelty remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section structure are retained. Local expansions explain backbone selection and endpoint-versus-path consistency; new appendix subsections move Additional Visual Results from B.6 to B.8. Author order, affiliations, contribution notes, publication header, and acknowledgements are also updated.

P2.justification: Four new tables (5 and 10–12) and expanded Tables 1–3 substantially enlarge the experimental displays. Figure 3 replaces zero filling with DDS and rearranges panels; Figure 7 expands from two to three training-curve panels. Existing supplementary reconstruction images are retained, with surrounding layout and placement adjusted.

improvement.justification: The DDS/FSBM comparisons, low-data studies, and discretization analysis strengthen empirical validation and document the N = 12 choice absent from v1. The gains are qualified: cross-anatomy KIDOT receives degraded target-domain training data unavailable to the supervised baseline, limiting the stronger generalization attribution, and uncertainty analysis is not extended to new results. Overall, these provide a useful but limited quality improvement.
